title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft sheet (header 'n° 393 – 35 –'), reused as scrap paper and photographed upside down. The neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's handwritten notes on Dieudonné modules, Barsotti–Tate (BT) groups, Tate's full-faithfulness theorem and the 'foncteur mystérieux'. This sheet has nothing to do with them. Its content is a set of exercises for Bourbaki's 'Théories spectrales' (Banach algebras, Ch. I).

Exercise 21: pseudo-resolvents in a unital Banach algebra A. Let R: Δ → A (Δ open in ℂ) satisfy the resolvent identity R(λ) − R(μ) = −(λ−μ)R(λ)R(μ).
(a) R has a local power-series expansion in powers of R(λ0).
(b) The n-th derivative is (−1)^n n! R(λ)^{n+1}.
(c) If R is holomorphic at infinity, write R(λ) = Σ c_n λ^{−n}. The identity forces c0 = z with z² = 0, c1 = j idempotent with zj = jz = 0, and c2 = x ∈ jAj. Then R(λ) = z + jR(λ,x), i.e. a nilpotent part plus the resolvent of x in the corner algebra jAj.
(d) R is the resolvent of some element of A iff R(λ0) is invertible for one λ0.
(e) Conversely, for any x the series Σ(λ0−λ)^n x^{n+1} is a pseudo-resolvent near λ0.

Exercise 22: the Cohen–Hewitt factorization theorem.
(a) Technical lemma: if u is an approximate left unit for w, then y = [(1−γ)e + γu]^{-1} (with 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1/4C) is also one.
(b) If A has a left approximate identity bounded by C, then every z ∈ A factors as z = xy, with y in the closure of Az and close to z. The hint builds the factorization recursively in the unitization Ã.
errors: 21a as transcribed requires |λ−λ0|·‖R(λ)‖ < 1 but expands R(λ) in powers of R(λ0). The identity actually gives R(λ0)(e + (λ0−λ)R(λ)) = R(λ). Under the stated condition this yields an expansion of R(λ0) in powers of R(λ), not the stated one. For the stated expansion of R(λ), the natural condition is |λ−λ0|·‖R(λ0)‖ < 1. Either the image reads R(λ0) or the draft has a slip.
22b: δ appears in the conclusion ‖z − y‖ < δ without being introduced. It should read 'for every δ > 0' (or ε).
21c hint: 'pour |λ| > λ0' mixes a radius with the point λ0 (a minor notational slip).

ideas.what: Pseudo-resolvents satisfying the resolvent identity; structure at infinity (nilpotent part plus resolvent in a corner algebra jAj); criterion for being a true resolvent
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Théories spectrales Ch. I exercises (Bourbaki draft, not Grothendieck)

ideas.what: Factorization z = xy in a Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity

deep.surprise_reason: This is the verso of a Bourbaki typescript draft (n° 393) on standard Banach-algebra exercises, reused as scrap paper. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics and is unrelated to the surrounding crystalline and p-adic notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down in the image; it is the back of a Bourbaki draft, 'n° 393', page 35.
'unipollente' is very likely 'unifère' (Bourbaki's term for unital).
In 21a, check whether the condition reads ‖R(λ0)‖ rather than ‖R(λ)‖.
In 22b, '‖z − y‖ < δ' presumably refers to an arbitrary δ > 0.
